evidence: The issue asks for time_sent to be populated and persisted. The agent read PasswordReset.send_email, which sets time_sent and calls save unconditionally, and saw its test mock save and check the call. It still made save conditional on not _state.adding to keep the old EmailVerification test passing, so the new test's save.call_count == 1 fails. It also changed Meta.ordering, which the issue never asks for.

The cause is that Request urlparses local filenames, so URL delimiters cut the path. The gold patch skips urlparse for URI_FILENAME. The agent swaps '#' for a placeholder and still calls urlparse, so in the test name the '?' splits off a query and the extension is '.()' instead of '.jpg'. Fixing the cause instead of one symbol was inferable from the issue.

The issue reports that list_spreadsheet_files now returns (files, response) and asks that the return type be documented and the change noted in HISTORY.rst. The agent kept the tuple, documented it, and added a module-level gspread.list_spreadsheet_files that returns the list. The test requires Client.list_spreadsheet_files itself to return a list, which is the revert the gold patch makes. The issue supports both documenting and reverting, and the tests pin the revert.

The gold patch performs substitution before factor filtering for every section. The agent instead filters factors inside the Replacer only when the target env name is not in default_factors, a special case built around the issue's [testenv:sub]. Both FAIL_TO_PASS tests substitute into [testenv:py27], where py27 is a default factor, so the raw factor lines survive. The run ended at the 100-turn limit; the self-check covered the sub case only.

At the base commit parse_update already sets _ready on every ok update. The issue's snippet sets _ready only when the id is not updateAuthorizationState, and the gold patch does the same. The agent kept the unconditional _ready.set() and only made the return value depend on the id. The new test checks that an updateAuthorizationState result stays not ready, which fails. The agent's verification script expects the auth result's wait() to succeed, which asserts its own patch.

The issue names the fix it would accept: an __eq__ on ElGamalCiphertext, which is what the gold patch adds. The agent wrote six reproduction scripts and never edited src/electionguard. The run ended at the 100-turn limit, so the recorded patch has scripts only.

The gold patch raises ValueError so the existing except branch assigns the np.nan object. The agent catches ZeroDivisionError, sets visibility = np.nan, and the next line converts it with units.Quantity(...).m_as('meter'), which yields a different NaN object. The test compares whole Metar tuples, where NaN fields match only by identity, so a correct NaN visibility fails. The note for fooled_reason: the patch does what the issue asks and the test depends on NaN identity.

The issue gives the fix: before a pop, move head bits into the tail until head is below precisions * ((2^32 // precisions) << 32), and undo that at the end of push. The agent's pop pulls bits from the tail when head is too large, and its push adds the undo step before the encode instead of after. Its final run of reproduce_bug.py printed 'BUG REPRODUCED' and the run ended at the 100-turn limit.

The issue states that without carbon all elements, hydrogen included, sort alphabetically. The agent's no-carbon branch puts one-letter symbols before two-letter ones, and its comment says this is to match the old test, which expected ['H', 'Ge', 'Si']. The new test expects ['Ge', 'H', 'Si'] for HGeSi, which the issue's rule gives.

The issue asks that TaxedMoneyField be a Django Field. The agent changed only the base class to models.Field and kept the old __init__, which does not call super().__init__, so the instance has no creation_counter. Both tests compare fields by creation_counter through Field.__lt__ and __eq__, which then fail. A Field subclass that ran Field.__init__ would have passed, so the failure comes from the half-built subclass, not from the issue.

The issue says Postgres and Trino are both 1-indexed. The gold patch sets INDEX_OFFSET = 1 on Postgres. The agent claimed Presto is 0-indexed and set INDEX_OFFSET = 0 on Trino's parser and generator, leaving Postgres at 0. The test transpiles Postgres col[1] to Hive, Postgres and Presto, so the Presto and Hive outputs stay wrong.

Since tox 4.0.13, expand_factors treats any line with a colon as a factor filter, so '8000:8000/tcp' is dropped or rewritten. The gold patch requires a space after the colon. The agent changed only line-ending normalization in str_convert.py, which the factor tests never reach. The run ended at the 100-turn limit, and its scripts tested list splitting, a different code path from the one at fault.

The gold patch makes find_root_task drop a cached root task that is done and search again, so workers are tied to the live task. The agent left find_root_task alone and filtered idle workers by loop.is_closed(). In the test the same loop runs run_until_complete three times and is never closed, so the worker bound to the first, finished task is still reused.

The issue says unknown atoms should be removed either by CanonicalizeModifications or by a separate processor. The agent chose the separate processor and changed CanonicalizeModifications to log and continue. The test runs only CanonicalizeModifications and expects the atoms gone, so it pins the other design. The agent's log in CanonicalizeModifications is at ERROR where the test wants WARNING, a second cause that precedence ranks below this one.

The agent builds ZipInfo(str(filename)) and sets external_attr = (S_IMODE(mode) << 16) | (mode & 0o170000). The file-type bits land in the low 16 bits, so stat.filemode(external_attr >> 16) gives '?r-x------' instead of '-r-x------'. Bare ZipInfo also dates every member 1980-01-01, while the old writestr(str) call used the current time, so the test's date check fails too. The gold patch uses ZipInfo.from_file, which keeps both.

The issue asks for the JPEG comment to show in im.info and gives no key or value format. The agent stores info['comment'] as the comment with trailing NULs stripped and decoded to str. The test expects the raw bytes b'File written by Adobe Photoshop\xa8 4.0\x00'. The plugin keeps raw bytes in app['COM'], which points toward bytes, but nothing in the issue or the code rules out a decoded string, so the format is not inferable with confidence.

The issue's title is 'Release v0.5.9', but its list says to update the version numbers from 0.5.7 to 0.5.8. The workspace already has 0.5.8 everywhere, so the agent fixed only the pyyaml constraint and lock and left the version alone. The test asserts __version__ == '0.5.9'. The issue contradicts itself on exactly the value the test checks.

The issue's stated expectation is that a second register_open call must not grow Image.ID. It also floats, as a 'probably', moving the readers of ID to OPEN.keys(). The agent did only that and removed the FitsStub ID.remove call, so register_open still appends every time. The test checks len(Image.ID) after re-registering JPEG, which is the expectation the issue states first.

The issue lists three strategies in one line each and says to use Yield and %Q30. The tests pin the sample UDF 'Required Yield (Gb)', the artifact UDF 'RE Coverage', methods named delivered and processed, exact comments such as 'AR: Delivered', and a move from aggregate/ endpoints to run_elements and samples with aggregated.* fields. None of these follow from the issue or the workspace. The agent's patch also stubs delivery detection with return False, but no reading of the issue reaches the tested names. Its checks assert its own reading of the strategies.

click.edit takes an extension argument for the temporary file, which the gold patch passes. The agent passed filename=f'temp{extension}' instead, which makes click edit a file named temp.rst in the working directory, ignore the initial text and return None. The tests expect click.edit(text, extension='.rst'), '.md' or '.txt'. The agent edited the existing test_create.py assertions to expect filename='temp.rst', so its self-check asserts its own call.
